Compliance workflow

Bulk TIN validation

Upload a workbook, confirm its mandatory headers, then validate each row against the embedded OECD country and taxpayer-type format rules.

.xlsx · pre-formatted as text

Drop an XLSX or XLSB workbook here

Click anywhere in this panel to choose a file · first sheet is used · data never leaves this browser

Required headers
Exact header names UCIC, Individual or Entity, Country of Tax Residence, CTR code, TIN value, TIN validation remarks, TIN Modification Remarks, TIN Value Modified, TIN validation remarks on Modified TIN value, these header are mandatory & checked before processing.
Taxpayer type
The Individual or Entity column accepts Individual or Proprietorship (individual rules) and Entity or Non-Individual (entity rules). Case, spacing and hyphens are ignored, so INDIVIDUAL and non individual both work.
Safe correction
Only punctuation and whitespace edits are suggested; source values remain unchanged. Progressive processing and a windowed preview keep the dashboard responsive at 10 lakh rows.

Scope, limits and standing notices

The sign-in prevents accidental access only — it is not a security control and does not protect the contents of this file. The credential is held in plain text inside this document and is readable in any text editor. Protect the file itself with disk encryption and OS file permissions.

This engine checks structure, not existence. A TIN reported as valid matches a format published in the OECD dataset for that jurisdiction and taxpayer type. It is not a confirmation that the number was ever issued, that it belongs to the named person, or that it is currently active. Jurisdictions that publish no format are reported as such and accept any value.

Session data is held in memory only: refreshing or closing this tab clears the signed-in name and any bulk results that have not been exported.
